body:
Adds four exhibits numbered §161–164 using the existing exhibit conventions and integrates repaired PR #1 at `663cbffe736b88353ac4d17ecff300c5d6ae665e`. The original 160 canonical entries match PR #1 exactly; its nine-entry modern allowlist and shared Historical Only definition remain intact.

| # | Exhibit | Canonical trust | Interactive |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 161 | NEMA — Swiss Rotor Machine | Historical Only | Historical military A–D wiring, drive wheels 12–15, red wheel 22/1, ten editable starting windows; encrypt/decrypt resets the machine |
| 162 | Hagelin C-36 / C-52 Lineage | Broken | Cross-links the M-209 demo; distinguishes variants, published attacks, and Crypto AG history |
| 163 | Fleissner Turning Grille | Broken | Editable 4×4, 6×6 and 8×8 masks; clockwise 90° rotations; reversible transposition with retained X padding |
| 164 | Myszkowski Transposition | Broken | Repeated-rank keyword, visible grid, encrypt/decrypt, incomplete final rows without padding |

All four use the canonical manifest and shared definitions, including generated headers, hall/map badges, search records, and artifact cards. M-209, Cardano Grille and Columnar Transposition have reciprocal cross-links. Map, halls, search, sitemap, README catalog, artifact metadata, and the **service-worker CORE list include all four HTML pages**; the three demo assets are also precached. The final generated version is **`cipher-museum-9bf65fa0`**. Counts are 144 cipher exhibits + 17 Foundations + 3 protocols = 164, retaining Foundations §141–157 and protocols §158–160. All 147 artifact cards retain their 1,323 existing descriptive fields; classification/history fields use repaired canonical data.

Historical verification:

- **NEMA:** production began in 1946 and service in 1947; four wired rotors, a moving reflector, and separate drive wheels. The military **17,576-step period is not the key space**; wheel selection, pairing and starting positions supply separate choices, and the demo fixes one wheel configuration. Verified against [Crypto Museum’s measured hardware and Swiss documentation](https://www.cryptomuseum.com/crypto/nema/index.htm).
- **Hagelin:** C-36 belongs to the 1930s five-pinwheel family; C-38/M-209 and C-52/CX-52 differ in wheels, lugs and stepping. C-52 dates to around 1952; there is no single key-space figure asserted for the entire lineage. Verified against [C-36 hardware](https://www.cryptomuseum.com/crypto/hagelin/c36/index.htm), [Crypto AG’s 2009 family history](https://www.cryptomuseum.com/crypto/hagelin/files/en_crypto_mag_1_09.pdf), and [Wessel’s hardware/document research](https://www.cryptomuseum.com/pub/files/BW_C52_CX52.pdf). [Greenough’s original 1999 paper](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/0161-119991887801) confirms the known-plaintext attack on irregular pinwheel stepping. [Crypto AG history and documentary references](https://www.cryptomuseum.com/crypto/hagelin/index.htm) support CIA/BND ownership from 1970; the exhibit does not project that claim onto every earlier C-36.
- **Turning grille:** Fleissner’s 1881 book and German WWI use are supported by [the original book](https://books.google.com/books/about/Handbuch_der_Kryptographie.html?id=Re_e13lww5IC) and [Friedman’s 1935 military text, pp. 28–30](https://www.nsa.gov/Portals/75/documents/news-features/declassified-documents/friedman-documents/publications/FOLDER_235/41760719079986.pdf), which records German use in 1915. [De Leeuw’s archival research](https://ep.liu.se/ecp/149/012/ecp18149012.pdf) documents Van der Harst’s 1913 probable-word break. A valid even-sided mask chooses one cell per four-cell rotation orbit: the 4×4 demo has **4⁴ = 256 starting hole patterns** with its fixed direction/readout. This is transposition; Cardano’s fixed mask is steganography.
- **Myszkowski:** [BnF’s original-book catalog](https://catalogue.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cb31000990s) confirms Paris, 1902. [ACA’s published rules and BANANA example](https://www.cryptogram.org/downloads/aca.info/ciphers/Myszkowski.pdf) confirm unique columns downward and tied columns across each row. The key is its width and ordered repeated-rank pattern; no unsupported fixed key-space bit count is claimed.

Known-answer vectors all encrypt correctly and decrypt back to the plaintext, including through live UI controls:

| Demo | Key/configuration | Plaintext | Ciphertext |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NEMA | A/12, B/13, C/14, D/15; red 22/1; windows MQQPZQSOEV | A repeated 27 times | HRSBVOOTZUCRWLMGRMGVWYWOVNF |
| Turning grille | 4×4; zero-based holes 0,1,2,5; clockwise; row-major readout | ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP | ABCEMDFGNOIHPJKL |
| Myszkowski | TOMATO; ranks 4,3,2,1,4,3 | WEAREDISCOVEREDFLEEATONCE | ROFOACDTEDSEEEACWEIVRLENE |

NEMA is pinned to the [independent rmsk2 test](https://github.com/rmsk2/rmsk2/blob/master/nema_test.cpp); Myszkowski is additionally checked against ACA’s full BANANA example. Grille padding is retained because genuine trailing Xs cannot be distinguished without the original length. Hagelin links to a related M-209 simulation rather than claiming it simulates all C-36/C-52 variants.

Validation at `1e190e0e7d347e5684d36a40827e602ac821045d`, using supported **Node 22.23.3**:

- All required generators ran; regeneration is idempotent. Trust/search/artifact/count/minified/service-worker freshness checks pass.
- `npm test`: **every suite passed**, including all suites after the timing guard; **85 engines measured, zero skipped, zero scaling violations**. The quadratic canary measured **16.09×** and was rejected by the unchanged 10× bound.
- Corpus replay: **100,026 records; 99,500 pass, 526 documented known deviations, zero unexplained deviations**.
- `npm run lint:html`: **201 files, zero errors**; `git diff --check`: clean.
- Historical-exhibit tests pass independent vectors, round trips across 0–100 letters, invalid keys, retained padding, interactive controls, all registrations, reciprocal cross-links and numbering.
- Four additional isolated deliberate mutations were rejected: wrong NEMA wiring, reversed grille rotation, wrong Myszkowski tie order, and missing Hagelin offline registration.
- Fresh committed LF checkout: service-worker version, complete 164-entry rendered trust audit, metadata freshness and historical-exhibit tests pass.

The earlier 37/40 timing failure and later 41/40 pass were environment-sensitive coverage, not a resolved engine regression. PR #1 now repairs the measurement logic and requires every engine; this branch inherits that repair.

Depends on [PR #1](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/cipher-museum/pull/1). **Keep this PR based on `fix/trust-label-audit`, open and unmerged; do not retarget to main yet.**
title: feat: add NEMA, Hagelin, turning grille, and Myszkowski exhibits
